title: GTA 6 Productivity: 18% of Surveyed US Workers Plan a Day Off
desc: BambooHR survey: 18% of US workers plan GTA 6 launch day off, and PTO requests run nearly 13% above past years. The $1B loss claim has no published study.
keywords: gta 6 productivity, gta 6 sick day, gta 6 calling in sick, gta 6 day off work, gta 6 pto requests, grand theft auto flu, gta 6 1 billion economy, gta 6 employers, gta 6 annual leave uk, gta 6 launch absenteeism
question: How many workers will take time off or call in sick for GTA 6, and what could it cost employers?
cta: Need customer replies covered when your team is short?
body:
Short answer. A real but limited share of staff plan to be away for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), which releases at midnight local time on November 19, 2026. In BambooHR's survey of 1,530 full-time US employees, 18% said they plan to take launch day off, and its platform data shows the PTO request rate for that Thursday running nearly 13% above the same day in 2024 and 2025. The widely shared claim that the launch will cost the US economy $1 billion has no published study behind it, so plan cover for Thursday and Friday rather than for a crisis.

On 16 November 2026 we read the original pages from BambooHR, One Day Agency, BrightHR, Logitech and Rockstar, plus official sick leave guidance, and traced the $1 billion figure through Fortune, MercoPress and the Guardian to a Cadena SER report from July 2025. Where only a news report exists, we say so. This is general information, not legal advice.

How many people plan to take time off for GTA 6

The most detailed US numbers come from BambooHR, an HR software company, in a data story dated October 22, 2026. It combines two sources, both published by BambooHR. The first is anonymized PTO data from more than 3.4 million US-based employees on its platform, pulled on October 19, 2026. The second is an online survey of 1,530 full-time US employees aged 18 or older, prepared by Method Research, distributed by RepData and collected from October 9 to 20, 2026.

What the survey found:

  • 18% of salaried workers, nearly 1 in 5, say they plan to take launch day off. The share rises to 32% of Gen Z workers and 27% of Millennials.
  • 50% of people planning time off for a new game release say they will call in sick rather than book PTO in advance.
  • 38% of all workers say calling in sick is easier than planning PTO, and 51% say they use sick time for things other than being sick.
  • 69% say they have worked while sick because taking the time off did not feel worth it.

The platform data shows the rise spreads past Thursday. BambooHR also notes that PTO requests across 2026 are running about 2 to 4% above the past two years in general, so part of any rise is not about the game.

A BambooHR spokesperson told Money the rise could also reflect workers using their time off more freely, according to Fortune. Take-Two's chief executive, Strauss Zelnick, joked in April 2026 that a lot of people would call in sick on November 19, as the Guardian reported.

In the UK, BrightHR looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees at 70,000 UK businesses. Days off booked for Thursday, November 19, 2026 were up 7.89% on the Thursday before, against 2.51% for the same pair of Thursdays in 2025, and the game made up nearly 5% of the reasons staff gave for leave on launch day. BrightHR also values that leave at about £3.14 million on launch day, without giving a method; booked leave is time staff are already entitled to, so it is not necessarily money lost.

Where the 1.2 million UK workers figure comes from

The Guardian's November 15, 2026 piece on what headlines call "Grand Theft Auto Flu" noted that the UK's Daily Star cited an HR company claiming 1.2 million British workers would take annual leave for the game. The Daily Star credits CharlieHR, and a Workplace Journal report calls it research highlighted by CharlieHR. We could not find a CharlieHR page or press release with the figures.

The survey underneath is One Day Agency's. The marketing agency says it commissioned the study itself through the YouGov platform. Its page gives a sample of 1,000 respondents but does not state the country or the fieldwork dates; UK outlets report it as a UK survey. The results cover everyone asked, including people who do not expect to play:

  • 7% expect to book release day off, and 4% expect to book several days off.
  • 8% expect to change their working hours, and 6% expect to change or swap a shift.
  • 2% list calling in sick among their plans, but 15% say they would be likely to call in sick if they could not get the day off.
  • 20% say they would play during working hours if they were working from home that day.
  • 75% chose none of the listed changes.

On our arithmetic, the 1.2 million and the 2.1 million day-off figure match the 4% and 7% answers applied to about 30 million workers. One Day Agency itself warns that its percentages refer to all respondents and should not be read as shares of employees or gamers, so the 1.2 million is an extrapolation the survey's own authors advise against.

The $1 billion US loss estimate, checked

Fortune's November 10, 2026 report on Logitech repeated one estimate that the US economy could lose as much as $1 billion in productivity as 1.5 million workers skip work. We found no published study behind that figure.

  • The earliest version we found is a Cadena SER radio report from July 28, 2025. It says the US is expected to lose about $1 billion on the first day alone and quotes José García Montalvo, an economics professor at Pompeu Fabra University in Barcelona, on who is most likely to stay home. The text gives no sample, data or method.
  • MercoPress reported in August 2026 that the estimate does not come from a published study and that no full method has been published. It describes the calculation repeated by other outlets as about 1.5 million absences multiplied by a US worker's average yearly contribution to GDP, about $70,000.
  • Montalvo did not respond to Fortune or the Guardian, which calls the figures back-of-the-napkin math.

Those inputs do not produce $1 billion on their own. Spread $70,000 a year over 260 working days and one day is about $269 per worker; times 1.5 million absences, that is about $404 million. Reaching $1 billion would take about $667 per worker per day, so some other assumption is missing.

Economists also question the idea of a loss at all. Victor Matheson of the College of the Holy Cross told Fortune that most of these absences shift when people take leave rather than adding to it, and that $1 billion would be roughly 1% of one day's US output.

What GTA 6 absences could cost your business

For a single employer, the national figure is the wrong number to plan with. Your cost depends on three things you can measure yourself:

  • Who is out. Booked leave is time staff are entitled to and is usually already in your budget. The cost is the gap it leaves on a busy day.
  • How late you find out. If BambooHR's 50% figure holds for your team, half of the game-related absences will arrive as sick calls that morning, when cover is hardest to arrange.
  • What slips. Missed calls, slower replies, late orders and overtime for the people who are in.

A simple way to size it: if your team resembled BambooHR's sample, 18% of a 50-person salaried team would be 9 people. Multiply the expected gap by your own daily cost of cover, such as overtime, temporary staff or delayed work, and add any service targets you could miss.

How to handle GTA 6 leave requests fairly

BrightHR's chief executive, Alan Price, says there is no reason to turn down a request as long as it does not leave you short-staffed. CharlieHR's Ben Gateley, quoted by Workplace Journal, says clear policies, a view of who is off and some flexibility work best. In practice:

  • Treat a gaming request like any other personal reason, and do not rank reasons.
  • Apply your normal rule for clashes, such as first come, first served or a rota, and write it down.
  • Set a cut-off date for requests covering November 19 and 20, 2026, and answer quickly so people can plan.
  • Offer the options people say they want. In One Day Agency's survey, more respondents expected to change hours or swap shifts than to book several days off.
  • Consider a company-wide approach. Logitech announced Logi Game Day on November 10, 2026, a dedicated day off for staff to play games and its first company-wide gaming day, with a streaming event at its Americas headquarters in San Jose on launch day. Fortune reported that its 7,000 employees can use the day on launch day or at another time over the following year.

Sick calls on launch day: handling them fairly

A sick call on November 19 may be genuine. BambooHR found 69% of workers have worked while ill, so a policy that treats every launch-day absence as suspect can push sick people back to their desks. Handle launch day the way you handle any other day, and check local rules before asking for proof. In general terms:

  • United States. The Department of Labor says there is no federal requirement for paid sick leave; the FMLA requires unpaid leave for certain medical situations at covered employers. Some states and cities have their own paid sick leave laws, and some limit when you can ask for proof. In New York City, an employer can ask for documentation only when an employee uses more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off, and only if its written policy says so, according to the city's Protected Time Off Law FAQs.
  • United Kingdom. GOV.UK says employees off sick for 7 days or less do not need a fit note; the employer can ask them to confirm the absence when they return, which is called self-certification. A fit note is needed after more than 7 days in a row.
  • Everywhere. Apply the same rules to everyone, keep remarks about the game out of absence conversations, and raise any suspected misuse privately under your written policy. Speak to an employment lawyer before disciplining anyone.

Coverage planning for GTA 6 launch week

Rockstar's support page says GTA 6 releases at midnight local time on November 19, 2026, in all regions, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar opened digital pre-load on November 10. A midnight release on a Thursday means the first night of play runs into a working day. Plan for it:

  • Pull your leave calendar for November 19 to 22, 2026, and mark roles with no backup.
  • Name a cover person for each critical role and write the short handover they need.
  • Move non-urgent meetings, deadlines and product releases away from Thursday and Friday.
  • Set an on-call rota for the weekend if your business runs then; BambooHR's data shows requests up for Saturday and Sunday too.
  • For remote staff, agree on availability windows and reply times rather than adding monitoring. One Day Agency's 20% figure is a hypothetical answer, not measured behavior.
  • Look past this one game. BambooHR lists Avengers: Doomsday on December 18, 2026 as another date where 18% of workers plan a day off.

Keeping customer response times up

Customers do not see who is off; they see how long a reply takes. A few steps keep service steady when a team is thin:

  • Post your support hours and expected reply times for launch week.
  • Turn on an automatic acknowledgment for email and chat that says when a person will reply and links to your main help articles.
  • Prepare saved replies for common questions, so whoever is covering answers the same way.
  • Route urgent topics, such as payments, outages and orders, to the people on shift, and queue routine questions with a clear time promise.

When the team is short, automated first responses that answer simple questions and pass the rest to a person can keep customer replies running; our AI automation page describes the chatbots and automated replies we build for customer service.

A checklist for November 19, 2026, and after

  • Check your leave and sick policies against the law where your staff work.
  • Tell staff how to request leave and the cut-off date for launch week.
  • Decide requests in policy order and answer in writing.
  • Confirm cover for every critical role on November 19 and 20, 2026.
  • After launch week, compare absences with the same week last year and plan the next big release from your own numbers.
faqs: Will people call in sick for GTA 6?

Some say they will. In BambooHR's survey of 1,530 full-time US employees, collected October 9 to 20, 2026, 50% of people planning time off for a new game release said they would call in sick rather than book PTO in advance. In One Day Agency's survey of 1,000 people through the YouGov platform, 2% listed calling in sick among their release plans, while 15% said they would be likely to if they could not get the day off.
How many people are taking the day off for GTA 6?

BambooHR found that 18% of US salaried workers plan to take launch day, November 19, 2026, off, and that the PTO request rate for that day on its platform of more than 3.4 million US employees is nearly 13% higher than comparable Thursdays in 2024 and 2025. In One Day Agency's survey, which UK outlets report as a UK survey, 7% of respondents expected to book the day off, and BrightHR saw days off booked for November 19 rise 7.89% on the Thursday before.
Will GTA 6 cost the US economy $1 billion?

No published study supports that figure. The earliest version we found is a Cadena SER radio report from July 2025 quoting economist José García Montalvo, with no method. MercoPress says the calculation repeated by other outlets multiplies about 1.5 million absences by about $70,000 of yearly output per worker; on our arithmetic, one working day of that is about $404 million. Economist Victor Matheson told Fortune that such absences mostly shift when leave is taken.
Where does the figure of 1.2 million UK workers come from?

The Daily Star credited CharlieHR, and Workplace Journal called it research highlighted by CharlieHR. The underlying survey is One Day Agency's, with 1,000 respondents through the YouGov platform, in which 4% expected to book several days off. Applying that 4% to a base of about 30 million workers gives 1.2 million, but One Day Agency warns its percentages should not be read as shares of employees.
Can an employer ask for proof of a sick day on GTA 6 launch day?

It depends on where your staff work. The US has no federal paid sick leave requirement, but some states and cities set rules; New York City, for example, allows documentation only for more than three consecutive workdays of protected time off and only if the written policy says so. In the UK, staff off sick for 7 days or less can self-certify. This is general information, not legal advice.
Is Logitech giving employees a day off for GTA 6?

Logitech announced Logi Game Day on November 10, 2026, a dedicated day off for employees to play games and its first company-wide gaming day, with a streaming event at its San Jose office on November 19, 2026. Fortune reported that its 7,000 employees can take the day on launch day or at another time over the following year.
